competitors.name: Toothsi (MakeO)
competitors.what: Indian D2C 3D-printed clear aligner startup founded 2018 with at-home scanning and teledentistry
competitors.funding_then: Raised $20M Series B led by Eight Roads Ventures in Aug 2021

competitors.name: Invisalign (Align Technology)
competitors.what: The clear aligner category leader that the 2021 Indian aligner startups positioned against on price
competitors.traction_then: Described as having popularised aligners in the West (YourStory, April 2021)

pivots.from: Snazzy, D2C clear aligners in India (YC W21, seed Dec 2021)
pivots.why: Not stated in any source found; the YC job page still carries Snazzy dental-tech text under the RocketSDR profile, and a YC profile exists at /companies/snazzy

target_customer: At the W21 batch: Indian consumers wanting affordable clear aligners (direct to consumer). Today: B2B companies doing outbound sales.
problem: At founding (as Snazzy): clear aligners in India cost more than INR 2 lakh and needed many clinic visits. Today: outbound sales research and outreach is manual and slow.
business_model: Founding business: D2C clear aligners made in-house with teledentistry (as Snazzy). Current business: B2B SaaS AI sales outreach platform.
product_category: D2C dental tech (clear aligners) at founding; sales development automation now

founders.name: Ayush Pateria
founders.background_notes: YC page: 'Hacker and entrepreneur'. Business Today (2021-12) names him and Chouksey as IIT Hyderabad graduates; Entrepreneur India calls him co-founder and CEO of Snazzy.

technical_complexity.rationale: As Snazzy: in-house 3D-printed aligners plus remote scanning and teledentistry across clinics in three cities (Business Today 2021-12): physical manufacturing and clinical operations on top of software. Judged for the original aligner business.

defensibility.rationale: Aligner pricing and teledentistry were being copied by at least Toothsi and Zenyum-type players in 2021; no patents or exclusive clinical network evidenced. For the current outbound tooling, the category is crowded and easily copied.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No source shows Align or others copying or buying Snazzy. The company is now listed as RocketSDR, so the aligner business seems to have been dropped; no source gives the date or reason.

market_need_then: Business Today (2021-12) quotes the clear aligners market at over $35B and says Snazzy's revenue doubled in the quarter and it was 'profitable on every order'; Entrepreneur India says existing aligners cost over INR 2 lakh. These are company claims.

branding.domain_note: rocketsdr.ai (current). Earlier Snazzy domain history not found.

identity.voice_and_tone: Snazzy: consumer-friendly ('we make people smile more'); RocketSDR: bold, confident ('Outbound that thinks for itself')

rebrands.why: Not sourced; accompanied by a change from D2C aligners to sales software

brand_strength.rationale: Snazzy got launch press in India for its seed (Business Today, Entrepreneur India, Inc42) but the company later became RocketSDR, whose name is easily confused with other 'Rocket' companies (a $15M-seed Indian AI app builder named Rocket appears in searches); no press about the brand itself.

outcome_analysis: RocketSDR, YC W21, began as Snazzy, a direct-to-consumer clear aligner company that raised a $2.2M seed in December 2021 from YC, Form Capital, Goodwater and ANIM Fund and claimed doubling revenue and profit on every order. It now appears under the name RocketSDR as an AI sales outreach platform, so the aligner business seems to have been dropped; no source gives the date or the reason. A later $5M Series A reported once is unverified. Listed Active with about 30 people, so the outcome is unresolved.
notes: Important: the W21 company was Snazzy (clear aligners); the YC page for RocketSDR shows no earlier name, but a YC job post under it and a /companies/snazzy URL, Business Today, Entrepreneur India and Inc42 coverage tie the founders and name together. The pivot date and reason are not found. Siliconindia reports a $5M Series A, and CB Insights lists total funding of $2.33M; neither verified, so only the seed is recorded and coverage is partial. Competitor dates: Toothsi source is Aug 2021 (after the batch, but the company was founded 2018); Zenyum not listed because its source date is unclear. Seedtable and Inc42 pages were not opened (403 for seedtable). The earlier depth-1 outcome text assumed an always-SDR product, which was wrong. Name origin not found.
